item: 2.3, definition of the exterior derivative on a manifold
description: The first image of a chart is printed as φ_α(U), not φ_α(U_α); retained as printed.
The codomain of the inclusion-induced map is printed as H(M), with no superscript k; retained.
The first rectangle I is printed as a rectangle in ℍ without a superscript n, unlike the preceding display; retained.
The first sum is printed with lower bound j=i and summand b_i T_i(v); retained.
The nonvanishing summand is printed as γ_i(q), although the bump functions are denoted γ_{p_i}; retained.
An integral-shaped glyph precedes K_{i+1} in the support condition, although the sentence calls the set open; glyph retained.
The distance threshold in K_i is printed as 1/n, not 1/i; retained.
The chart is printed as x:V→ℝ without a superscript n; retained.
The text gives p∈c(I) and V(0)=v, without explicitly requiring c(0)=p; retained as stated.
The printed Φ_T has domain V*×V* although the following arguments v,w are in V; both retained.
The time range in c_av(t)=c_v(at) is printed t∈I, although J was introduced as the inverse image of I under multiplication by a; retained.
The author in entry Hel01 is printed as Helgasson, S.; retained without normalizing the name.
The original prints ‘formula (9)’ without an actionable target. The manuscript retains (9) and links to the source occurrence only; no translated formula is assigned as its target.
The expansion shows a plus at the end of one line and another at the beginning of the next. The two printed continuation signs are retained.

item: Proof of Theorem 4.3, citation of Poincaré lemma
description: The original cites Exercise 3.8(5), while the statement called the Poincaré lemma appears under (6)(h). The source's printed reference is retained and links to item (5).
The printed formula for φ(x,y) uses ψ_{1,x} and ψ_{2,x}, with the same parameter x; retained.

The printed text cites ‘Sect. 4.5 of Chap. 1’; its original PDF link leads to the current Chapter 4 section, not Chapter 1. The translated citation links to the original occurrence without assuming a corrected target.

item: 4.5, discussion of normal curvature following Example 5.5
description: The paragraph begins with M=ℝ^{n+1}, but the metric in the covariant-acceleration sentence is stated to be the Euclidean metric in ℝ³; both dimensions are retained.
The number of particles is denoted by k in the prose, whereas the upper bound of the kinetic energy sum is printed as n. Both are retained.

item: 5.3, paragraph below the principal-axis Euler equations
description: The original calls P constant in the body frame immediately before displaying a differential equation for P. The parenthetical adjective and the equation are both retained.
The original first states Ω=I^{-1}P, then writes Ω=I_iP and ω=I_ip for equilibrium points. The factors are retained as printed.
The displayed kernel equality uses q, but the text below quantifies over p in U. The two letters are retained; Exercise 4.15(1) uses q as printed there.
The first term in the expansion of dH/dt uses a double index i,j although j does not occur in the summand. The printed sum is retained.
The printed expression for F_y/m ends in =0. The last equality is retained exactly as printed.

item: Proof of Theorem 6.12, piecewise definition on cotangent bundle
description: The source writes the auxiliary function as an element of C∞(M), although its argument is a covector on T*M. The printed function space is retained.
The source uses p_r on the left of both Legendre transformation identities; the second identity differentiates with respect to the angular velocity. The two printed subscripts are retained.
The upper bound in the sum for X_F is printed as p, whereas the coordinate indices in (a) run to n. The printed upper bound is retained.
The Hamiltonian is printed as H:T*Q→ℝ, even though its displayed coordinates and subsequent invariance claim refer to T*M. The displayed domain is retained.
The displayed center subspace lists w through w_{n_c}, but the following prose ends the same list at w_{n_s}; it also states E^c=∅. These printed expressions are retained.

Chapter 5 has a distinct Warner entry with a different publication city. After integrating the chapter references, the citation key was redirected to bib:ch05-War83 without changing the translated prose.
The source writes x:ℝ⁴→ℝ for an inertial frame. The printed domain and range are retained; Section 6.1 defines an inertial frame as a diffeomorphism to ℝ⁴.
The printed parenthetical tangent-vector order is timelike, spacelike or null, whereas the preceding listing is timelike, null or spacelike. Both printed orders are retained.

item: Exercise 4.3(6), twin paradox on a cylinder
description: The source cites Exercise 2.2(5), which is the car and garage paradox; the twin paradox is Exercise 2.2(4). The original printed reference is retained and links to item (5).
The printed paragraph says a particle cannot leave the region r=2m. The equality is retained without substituting an inequality.
The lift vector is printed as u†∈T_pU although the current exercise denotes the region by M. The printed symbol U is retained.
The first term in the displayed metric is printed with a positive A², unlike the earlier Schwarzschild ansatz. The printed sign is retained.
The printed concluding inequality W_p(t)<0 includes t=0 in [0,1], although the proof previously gives W_p(0)=0. The printed interval is retained.
The printed reference for the null vector parallelism assertion is Exercise 2.2(8) (generalized twin paradox). The translation links to that printed target without substituting another item.

The printed reference for the Ricci expansion points to Chapter 4 Section 6.1 (notes on constant curvature), where the cited expansion is not given. The translation retains the printed reference and does not substitute a target.
The printed proof defines s as the first focal point but subsequently says that q is conjugate to p. Both statements are retained as printed.
After applying the Penrose theorem, the printed example also names Theorem 8.9 (the Hawking theorem). The translation retains the printed target.
The printed cylinder and cone set builders list (x,y) while a third coordinate z is used. The translation retains the printed set builders.
The printed overlap W is expressed using the images of U_alpha and U_beta under Phi_alpha and Phi_beta, without the R^n factors that appear in the preceding union. This distinction is retained.

The printed solution says the derivative of the scalar-valued map is injective for x != 0 before invoking the regular value theorem. It also lists only x^1 through x^n as arguments on the left of the first display. Both were retained.
The derivation of C=-1/x_0 in the printed solution starts with x_0 in R and does not separately treat x_0=0. No separate argument was added.
The printed assertion h(R)=R minus zero is retained, even though the determinant of a real matrix exponential is positive.
The printed identity is sigma composed with sigma = sigma, although Exercise 8.6(9)(d) states the right hand side as the identity. The mismatch is retained.
The last display prints b without the subscript J in both coefficient terms, unlike the preceding expressions. The last display retains this distinction.
The printed formulas show both angular coordinates and the corresponding differentials as v. This repeated notation is retained rather than silently substituting a second letter.
The printed proof writes p_1,p_2 in S^2 in the general S^n case. The exponent 2 is retained.
The printed concluding line puts the multiplier f outside the entire parenthesis, unlike the preceding line. The formula is retained as printed.
The last tensor component in the displayed expansion has j_(k-1) before s, even though the corresponding outer sum and connection use m. The printed superscript is retained.
The printed proof first sends a point to (0,0,1), then specifies a neighborhood of (1,0,0); the comparison set goes from V to W. Both were retained.
The printed parenthetical calls the two tangent planes orthogonal even though the following sentence gives their common tangent line. The wording is retained.

High-resolution review of the accepted solution shows that the source distinguishes its two v glyphs by font but gives neither a bar. The current translation uses an explicit bar for the second variable. Leave the accepted source untouched while continuing, and review a narrow fidelity correction at final QA.
The evaluated component formula repeats j in the summation list although the integrand includes l. The printed indices are retained.

The source displays both real coordinate letters as v without an overbar; font encodings and original glyphs were inspected. It also says g maps H^2 onto itself in a discussion of the map f. Both are retained as printed.

Both printed coordinate glyphs map to v, and the saddle parameterization is printed as a map to R^2 even though it has three components. The printed notation is retained, not inferred from the mathematics.

The converse refers to numbered equation (7.29), the displayed chain rule, rather than the unnumbered proportional-acceleration equation. The printed target is retained as a verified internal equation link.
The printed y(t) formula uses theta rather than theta_0 in the sine term. The subscript is not added.
The signs and locations of singularities in the printed potential, limits and interval endpoints are not mutually consistent. Each is rendered as printed.
In the last displayed equation the printed plus sign stands between the contraction operator and d alpha. The order is preserved; the following subpart has the contraction in its usual position.
The printed return parameter is t_1/k notwithstanding the definition c(t)=gamma(t/k). The printed expression is retained.
The printed inverse-matrix definition repeats upper indices, and the displayed bilinear expression uses v in both factors. The printed indices and factors are retained.

The printed Example 5.4 reference is not a matching number in the original. The example giving the cotangent lift and its momentum map is linked to the verified target (Example 8.19 in the translated edition).
The two displayed fractions in solution (4) print a first-order numerator over a second-order denominator, unlike solution (2). Retained as printed.
The source references the numbered line for the time derivative, and later prints X with superscripts rather than the E frame used earlier in the solution. Both are retained.
The source prints Exercise 5.1. The matching exercise actually giving the radial first integrals is Section 6.5 Exercise (5)(b); the translated reference links to that exercise.

In (8) the printed standard metric is on S^3, and the final steps of (9)(c) print exponent -1/2. Both are retained. The printed Exercise 6.1 subparts (7) and (3) link to their verified topic matches in Section 6.6.
The source prints svpp h and (o, epsilon_0) in (4), and says timelike with a non-strict inequality and equality for the distance estimate in (8). These readings are retained.

The original PDF encodes both coordinate names as v in distinct glyph fonts (CMMI10 and MTMI), whereas the original exercise uses u and v. The solution distinguishes v and italic v without replacing one by u.
